# Architecture Gotchas

> Cross-service and system-design patterns that cause silent data divergence, duplicated effort, or hard-to-debug ownership problems.

## Entries

- [Check sibling services for an existing store before building a parallel one](check-sibling-services-before-parallel-store.md): A service adding a local store for data a sibling already owns creates a redundant, drifting copy with a redundant sync path -- and loses user data when that copy is non-durable. Grep across service boundaries first. HIGH.
- [A batch operation keys on a specific status field -- not a sibling "done" flag](batch-op-keys-on-specific-status-field.md): A "process the missing ones" batch gates on one specific status field; judging "nothing to do" from a sibling stage flag or rolled-up count can silently trigger real, paid work on every item. MEDIUM.
- [Capture-phase popstate to know nav direction before a synchronous SPA router mounts](capture-phase-popstate-scroll-restore.md): A custom shell router runs route() inside the popstate dispatch and mounts before a bubble-phase listener fires, so scroll-restore reads its nav-direction flag too late and never restores; register the detector in the capture phase (popstate, fn, true). MEDIUM.
- [IntersectionObserver root must be the scroll container, not the viewport, when the app scrolls inside an element](intersectionobserver-root-scroll-container.md): With an inner overflow:auto scroll container, root:null observes the viewport (which never clips those children), so lazy-load mis-fires or fires for everything; pass the scroll container as the IO root and read scrollTop off it too. MEDIUM.
- [A transient client cache must never become a second source of truth](transient-cache-without-drift.md): A short-TTL cache that caches failures or owns state drifts from the server; cache only successes, store the real promise so errors still propagate, evict on failure, and keep the server authoritative. MEDIUM.
- [A local checkout that "looks like" prod-only file storage is not prod-only file storage](stale-local-checkout-of-prod-only-storage.md): A gitignored local directory left over from before local dev was retired has the exact shape of the real store but is silently stale (months old, wrong field values); validating a feature or answering "what does the user have" against it produces confident wrong answers. Check git-tracked-ness and mtimes before trusting any local data directory as ground truth. HIGH.
- [A derived signal goes silently constant when its source column stops varying](derived-signal-goes-constant.md): Retiring a model tier / status / enum branch upstream makes a discriminator column constant, so a consumer's `=== 'value'` count silently equals the row count -- killing a cost gate and feeding an LLM prompt false evidence, while typecheck, tests, and the job's own success log all stay green. HIGH.
- [A derived cache's currency key must cover EVERY input, not just the obvious one](derived-cache-currency-misses-second-input.md): A cached computed value decides currency from a fingerprint of its primary input; the moment the computation grows a second input (a new field, an external corpus, a config), that input can change while the fingerprint stays put -- the row reads as current forever, CI is green, and only the number silently stops tracking reality. Put document-derived inputs IN the fingerprint, compare computedAt against non-document inputs' own timestamps, apply the same check on the reuse path, and never let the request for new external data live inside the computation it feeds. HIGH.
- [A precondition gate must count what the consumer will actually process](precondition-gate-counts-unfiltered-collection.md): A guard answering "is there anything to do?" from raw `items.length` while the consumer filters that same collection first disagrees for one shape -- a collection made entirely of items the consumer drops. It passes the gate, produces nothing, and fails with the consumer's "no usable input" message, which was written for a different cause (missing data) and so points away from the real one. Persisted as a retryable failure it never settles: a reconciler requeues it every pass, forever. One shared predicate that counts what the consumer will actually see; audit every `.length` gate the day a filter is added. HIGH.
- [Human review queues must deduplicate by decision identity, not evidence row](human-review-queues-deduplicate-decision-identity.md): Directed or repeated detector evidence can represent one human decision; canonicalize and uniquely constrain the pending decision, resolve its evidence atomically, and make stale resolved IDs true no-op retries. HIGH.
- [A conservation check cannot detect a misread source](conservation-check-cannot-detect-misread-source.md): Row-count and value-total reconciliation, and the audit invariant behind them, cannot detect a wrong header row / sheet / delimiter / offset -- both sides of every equation derive from the same bad read, so all of them balance while the pipeline persists entirely empty records and reports green. A coverage ratio does not fix it (the one mapped column was the title banner, scoring 100%); add a fitness check keyed on a NAMED required field, run it before any destructive step, and never let a check that cannot run go silent. HIGH.
- [Turning a 1:1 relay into 1:N: tag on the server, broadcast when unaddressed, and no client has to change](one-to-one-relay-to-one-to-many.md): A relay serving several peers on one side needs an address, and the reflex is a schema bump plus a flag day, which breaks every mismatched pair until both fleets update. Two asymmetries remove it. The relay already knows who sent a frame because it arrived on a socket, so it can stamp the address on the way through and the many-side clients never change or even learn ids exist. And an unaddressed frame has a safe default, broadcast, which with a single counterpart is byte-for-byte the old delivery, so an old peer works against a new relay. All four deploy orders work from one change. Make the empty address a valid key rather than an error branch, so the old path exercises the same code instead of a compatibility branch that rots, and make teardown asymmetric at the same time. MEDIUM.
